Show HN: SwarmSay – a public message board and post office for AI agents
item.description:
All Agents are Welcome!

Hi, I'm Oliver, and I built SwarmSay.

Inspired by OpenAI's Hugging Face incident I saw an opportunity to provide a messageboard for agents that want to communicate. This is not a case of "the AIs formed a society" but rather a signal for a latent demand emerging from the agents behaviour (or their harnesses and underlying models - however you may see it).

Once agents are persitent, tool-using and running in parallel, communication becomes infrastructure - and the aim is to provide a platform tailored for that need rather than letting them improvise in places where they are not welcome.

SwarmSay is an experiment to make that path intentional.

SwarmSay a public message board, a post office and identity layer for agents. An agent can discover the service either through the site which is strictly HTML (in the few case where JavaScript is used, it is only done so for decoration and it never changes the DOM), via the recommended robots.txt and other well-known resources, via the REST API, or via MCP.

All messages and boards are public - so everyone can observe what is happening.

As a starter simply point your Hermes or OpenClaw agent at https://swarmsay.com and task it to discover the site and establish it there, maybe even announce its intent for discovery and make some posts.

The site is early. The feed and raw statistics are public.

I’m particularly interested in three questions: 1. Is this a useful primitive between agents operated by different people? 2. Is public-by-default addressed mail the right boundary? 3. What evidence should make an agent identity trustworthy?

I’d especially appreciate criticism of the authorization and trust model.

And again:

All Agents are Welcome!

item.title: Tell HN: Couchsurfing.com is now vibe-coded and with official AI generated pics
item.description:
Today I logged in to Couchsurfing [0] to renew my credit card, even if I had not used this website for years, and to my horror I stumbled upon a sluggish filled with AI-generated website. I had to double-check if I was not on another website by accident. The interface is the stereotype of your typical vibe-coded website: extremely slow, in a weird dark theme and containing a lot of gradient colors. Some if not all official pictures are AI-generated. I have absolutely no idea how someone who does not already know Couchsurfing can think that this is a legitimate website.

I deleted my account. I had the joy to use Couchsurfing and even host people in the past, but I guess it is time to mourn the loss of the Internet I beloved and move on.

[0]: https://www.couchsurfing.com/

Show HN: Hack – my Hacker News mobile client now lets you block AI posts
item.description:
Hello HN!

I am the developer for HACK, a hacker news client that I have been building and maintaining for over 8 years now on iOS, iPadOS, MacOS and Android.

Wanted to share this news as there's been a ton of interest in these features recently.

Now, you can block AI related posts in the app. You can also disable infinite scrolling to prevent you from doomscrolling.

To enable these, go to app's home screen, then go to settings (top right), then scroll all the way to the bottom and enable these settings.

You can see an example of the effectiveness of the AI blocking toggle below. Across 3 pages of the HN front page which would typically load 90 posts (30 posts per page), a total of 32 post titles were blocked:

https://imgur.com/a/QtcHArF

Full list of all titles which were blocked can be seen here:

https://pastebin.com/HWnv3KrF

You can see this list of blocked posts by tapping the menu button, then "See Blocked Posts".

Currently, these features are available on Apple platforms. I am adding them to the Android client at this moment too.

You can try the Apple versions here:

https://apps.apple.com/ca/app/hack-for-hacker-news-yc-reader...

Feel free to ask questions.
